app.name: CaseFile Earth
app.tagline: Every trend is a suspect until the evidence says otherwise.
app.subtitle: Has rain or heat changed where you live, and is it changing differently from somewhere else?

banner.synthetic: Example data, not real measurements. Used only to build and test the site.
banner.offline: You are offline: showing the cases kept on this device.
banner.results_unreachable: Results are not reachable right now. The cases kept on this device still work.

home.hero_body: Pick a question and a place. We test whether temperature or rain really changed, using NASA data, and show the evidence.
home.learning_goal: In two minutes you can say how fast rain changed in two places, whether the two differ, and why “can't tell yet” is not “no change”.
home.credit_line: Built with NASA data: MERRA-2 (model) and GPM IMERG (satellites and gauges).

question.title: What do you want to find out?

place.title: Where?
place.pick_cell: Or pick any 1° cell on the screening map
place.cells_shown: Shaded squares are the data cells that cover this place.
place.not_in_set: This division is too small for the data grid, so it is not in our set.

lineup.title: What changed here?
lineup.intro: Temperature and rain, for the whole year and each season. {n_tests} tests on this screen.

headline.cant_tell_yet: Can't tell yet whether {variable} {in_region}{season_phrase} changed over {from}–{to}. That is not the same as no change.

verdict.total_pct: Total change over {from}–{to}: {total_signed} ({pct} of the starting level).

snr.small: That is smaller than the usual year-to-year ups and downs.
snr.similar: That is about as big as the usual year-to-year ups and downs.
snr.large: That is bigger than the usual year-to-year ups and downs.

sure.confirmatory: One of {family_size} tests we registered in advance; after correcting for all of them, {p_adj_expr}.
sure.secondary: A secondary result: one of {family_size} season tests registered in advance; after correcting for them, {p_adj_expr}.
sure.mkar1: Mann–Kendall test allowing for year-to-year memory, before correction: {p_expr}.
sure.below: That is below the {alpha} line we set in advance.
sure.above: That is above the {alpha} line we set in advance, so we can't tell yet.
sure.doubts: That is below the {alpha} line we set in advance, but {n_doubts} of our checks raise doubts, so we can't tell yet.

labels.practical: Is it big enough to matter?
labels.ttest: t-test with effective sample size (shown for comparison; it does not decide)

strong.name: Strong evidence
strong.desc: Clearly below our pre-set line, and none of our checks raises a doubt.

supported.name: Supported trend
supported.desc: Below our pre-set line after correcting for all our tests, with at most one doubt.

cant_tell_yet.name: Can't tell yet
cant_tell_yet.desc: This record can't tell. That is not the same as no change.

reason.outside_domain: No verdict: outside the range this method was tested for. The fitted rate is {rate} per decade.
reason.short_record: Exploratory: only {n} years ({from}–{to}). The fitted rate is {rate} per decade. No verdict.
reason.too_short: Too short to test: only {n} years.
reason.missing_year: No verdict: years are missing from this record ({years}). A verdict needs every year.
reason.not_testable: Not testable: the test could not give a valid result for this record.
reason.break_review: No verdict: a known change in the data shows as a step here ({label}).
reason.exploration: Exploration: {rate} per decade (95% range {lo} to {hi}). This is not one of our pre-registered tests, so it gets no verdict.
reason.sensitivity: Sensitivity check: {rate} per decade (95% range {lo} to {hi}) in IMERG, a second rain record. It is shown beside MERRA-2 and gets no verdict.

coverage.title: Did the data coverage change?
coverage.doubt: The share of the area with data changed over time ({cmin} to {cmax}); part of the trend could come from that.

breaks.title: Instrument or Earth?
breaks.none: No documented data change falls inside these years.
breaks.reviewed: A documented data change falls in {year} ({label}); a person checked and saw no step there.
breaks.unreviewed: A documented data change falls in {year} ({label}) and has not been checked by a person yet.
breaks.step: A documented data change in {year} ({label}) shows as a step, so we give no verdict.

loo.title: One unusual year?
loo.pass: No single year decides the answer.
loo.doubt: Remove {year} and the answer changes: one year matters a lot.
loo.note: Without {year} the result would look stronger; one year matters.

windows.title: Other start and end years?
windows.doubt: Only {agree} of {ran} other windows agree: the answer depends on the years chosen.
windows.label: Robustness checks, not new claims.

pettitt.title: A sudden jump?
pettitt.flag: A jump around {year} stands out (Pettitt test, a flag only: it does not change the verdict).

checks.model_note: This comes from a model that blends many observations (a reanalysis). Models can shift when the observations they use change.

practical.exceeds: We decided in advance that a change of {threshold} per decade matters. The whole 95% range is beyond that.
practical.overlaps: We decided in advance that a change of {threshold} per decade matters. The 95% range includes smaller changes, so it may or may not matter.
practical.smaller: We decided in advance that a change of {threshold} per decade matters. The whole 95% range is smaller than that.

overturn.O1: If the data change in {year} ({label}) turned out to be a step, this would be a change in the data, not in the Earth.
overturn.O2: The answer leans most on {year}: without it, {p_expr}.
overturn.O3: The weakest of the other windows, {from}–{to}, gives {rate} per decade.
overturn.O4: If year-to-year memory were stronger or slower than our model assumes, the test would be too eager. Our check found {finding} here.
overturn.O5: IMERG, a different rain record, points {direction} over {from}–{to}.
overturn.O6: Changes smaller than {threshold} per decade would not matter in practice; the 95% range {includes} them.
overturn.O7: A longer record or a larger region could change this answer.

contrast.title: Compare two places

headline.rates_differ: {Variable}{season_phrase} changed at different rates in {A} and {B}: the trend in the difference ({A} − {B}) is {rate_d} per decade (95% range {lo_d} to {hi_d}).
headline.cant_tell_yet: Can't tell yet whether {variable}{season_phrase} changed differently in {A} and {B}. That is not the same as no difference.
headline.no_verdict: No verdict on the difference between {A} and {B}: {reason}
headline.exploration: Exploration: the difference ({A} − {B}) changed by {rate_d} per decade (95% range {lo_d} to {hi_d}). This pair is not pre-registered, so it gets no verdict.
headline.sensitivity: Sensitivity check (IMERG): the difference ({A} − {B}) changed by {rate_d} per decade (95% range {lo_d} to {hi_d}). It is shown beside MERRA-2 and gets no verdict.

contrast.side: {A}: {rate_a} per decade (95% range {lo_a} to {hi_a}). {B}: {rate_b} per decade (95% range {lo_b} to {hi_b}).
contrast.opposite_fitted: The two fitted lines point in opposite directions. On its own that does not show the trends differ.
contrast.supported_opposite: Both places have supported trends, in opposite directions: supported opposite trends.
contrast.not_subtracted: Each place's own rate is shown beside the difference, never subtracted from it.

sensitivity.title: Sensitivity check: IMERG
sensitivity.lineage: Both records use rain-gauge and satellite inputs, so this is a sensitivity check, not an independent confirmation.
sensitivity.same: Over {from}–{to}, IMERG gives the trend in the difference the same sign: {rate_i} per decade (MERRA-2: {rate_m}).
sensitivity.other: Over {from}–{to}, IMERG gives the trend in the difference the opposite sign: {rate_i} per decade (MERRA-2: {rate_m}).

map.title: Screening map: where is it changing?
map.label: Screening map: exploration, not a verdict.
map.legend_dot: Dot: stands out after allowing for testing {n_tests} cells at once (false discovery rate 10%)
map.click_hint: Pick a cell to see its record.

cell.title: 1° cell at {lat}, {lon}
cell.exploration: A single cell is exploration only: it gets no verdict.

methods.title: How we know
methods.intro: Every number on this site comes from one tested piece of code. This page shows what it does and how well it works.
methods.coverage: How often the 95% range catches the true rate
methods.power: What a record this long can detect
methods.prereg: Pre-registration (committed before we looked at any trend)
methods.property: With no trend, it flags about {k} in 100 such records. This describes the method, not the chance that a verdict on this site is wrong.
methods.power_sentence: If year-to-year noise stays as it was, a change of {threshold} per decade would be caught in about {k} of 10 records this long.

offline.title: Cases kept on this device
offline.intro: These cases work with no internet. Everything else needs a connection.

errors.missing_file: This result is not in this build.
errors.bad_view: This link is incomplete; we filled in sensible defaults.

glossary.trend: A steady rise or fall over many years, not just one unusual year.
glossary.cant_tell_yet: The record is too short or too noisy to decide. It does not mean nothing changed.
glossary.p_value: How often random ups and downs alone would produce a trend at least this strong.
glossary.range_95: A range of rates that fit the data. Ranges made this way catch the true rate about 95 times in 100; it is not a 95% chance for this one range.
glossary.mann_kendall: A test that counts how often later years are higher than earlier years.
glossary.t_test: A test of whether the best straight line slopes more than noise would allow.
glossary.sen_slope: The middle value of all the slopes between pairs of years; one odd year cannot fool it.
glossary.memory: When one year resembles the next, the record holds less information than its length suggests.
glossary.difference: Region A minus region B, year by year. If the two changed at different rates, this difference has a trend.
glossary.pre_registered: Written down and committed before we looked at any trend, so we cannot pick the results we like.
glossary.exploration: Anything we did not register in advance. We show it, but give no verdict.
glossary.model: A computer model that blends many observations into a complete picture, such as MERRA-2.
glossary.satellite: A sensor in orbit that measures the Earth, such as the satellites behind IMERG.
